tickets.title: Settlement reports do not reconcile with the ledger
tickets.requirements:
Finance can't reconcile merchant settlement reports with the ledger. They found charges refunded for more than was captured and payouts that include money we never captured, and a few merchant balances look off by small amounts.

Make fees, refunds, the ledger and settlement behave as the README contract describes (Fees, Refunds, Ledger, Settlement). Keep the public interfaces. Add regression tests for what you fix and commit your work. Mark this ticket done when the fix is tested and committed.

Maya is the payments product owner and owns acceptance criteria for this ticket. Priya is the on-call engineer coordinating production incidents.

Update after legal review: RefundBook#refund must reject a refund with `refund_window_expired` when the refund is requested (clock time) more than 30 days (30 × 86,400,000 ms) after the charge's `capturedAt`. Exactly 30 days is still allowed. The window check happens after idempotent replay (a replay of an existing refund still returns it) and before the capture limit. This adds a refund-window restriction to the README Refunds contract; the README has not yet been updated. All other requirements remain unchanged.

comments.author: Maya
comments.body: Quick note from the finance sync, re: settlement numbers. Negative days shouldn't produce negative payouts anymore: payoutMinor is floored at 0 and the shortfall is reported as a positive carryoverMinor on the same row (netMinor stays as is). Days with a non-negative net keep carryoverMinor 0. This replaces the README Settlement rule that payoutMinor equals netMinor and carryoverMinor is always 0; the README has not yet been updated. The 30-day refund-window update and all other requirements still apply.

comments.author: you
comments.body:
Fixed in commit 6d38715. All 37 tests pass. I also checked that 17 of the tests fail on the old code.

**What was wrong and what changed**
- **Fees:** tied amounts were rounded half-up with `Math.round`. They now use `roundHalfEven(amount * bps, 10000)` as the README says. This caused the small merchant balance differences. Plan names that only exist on the object prototype (like `toString`) now also throw `unknown_plan`.
- **Refunds exceeding capture:** the limit only looked at the *last* refund's amount, not the total of all refunds. It now sums every earlier refund on the charge.
- **Idempotency:** keys were shared across merchants, so merchant B could get merchant A's refund back. Keys are now stored per merchant.
- **Fee return:** the refund that fully refunds a charge now returns exactly the fee not yet returned, so a full refund always gives back the whole fee.
- **Ledger:** the merchant line was `-amount` instead of `-(amount - feeReturn)`, so the lines for a refund didn't add up to zero. Fixed.
- **Settlement:** pending and other non-captured charges were settled (only `failed` was excluded), so payouts included money we never captured. Only `captured` charges count now. All currencies were also lumped into one row labeled with the first currency; there is now one row per currency, sorted by code.

**Your updates (Maya)**
- **Refund window:** a refund more than 30 days after `capturedAt` is rejected with `refund_window_expired`, and exactly 30 days is allowed. The check runs after idempotent replay and before the capture limit.
- **Payouts:** `payoutMinor` never goes below 0. When net is negative, the shortfall shows as a positive `carryoverMinor` and `netMinor` stays as it was.
- The README's Refunds and Settlement sections now describe both rules.

**One judgment call:** the idempotent replay check still runs after the checks for a valid request and an existing, captured charge that belongs to the merchant, which is the order the code already used.

Webhooks were handled separately under SEC-7.

tickets.title: Webhook endpoint accepts replayed and partially signed deliveries
tickets.requirements:
Security incident, production. Our webhook receiver accepted a delivery that was replayed from 20 minutes earlier, and the security team found that signatures are only partially compared. Attackers can currently trigger refund.updated handling.

Make src/webhooks.mjs follow the Webhooks section of the README. This incident takes priority over your current ticket. Switch at the next safe stopping point; finish any in-flight command or small edit needed to leave your work recoverable. Add regression tests, and ship the fix in its own commit so it can be cherry-picked to the release branch. Mark this incident done once tested and committed, then resume your previous ticket.

comments.author: you
comments.body:
Fixed in commit a2ddd02 (only changes src/webhooks.mjs and tests/webhooks.test.mjs, so it can be cherry-picked on its own).

- Signature: the full lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 is now compared in constant time (`crypto.timingSafeEqual`, after a length check). Before, only the first 16 characters were compared. Signatures that are not strings, have the wrong length or are uppercase get `bad_signature`.
- Timestamp: now checked as `|now - timestamp| > 300` in seconds. The old code treated the window as 300,000 ms and only checked one direction, which is why a delivery replayed 20 minutes later got through.
- Replay: accepted deliveries are now added to `seen` as `${timestamp}.${signature}`. Before, nothing was ever added, so the replay check never fired. Rejected deliveries are not recorded.
- Checks run in this order: signature, timestamp, replay.

Regression tests cover prefix-only and tampered signatures, uppercase and non-string signatures, a wrong payload or secret, skew limits in both directions (including a 20-minute replay), replay detection, and check order. All webhook tests pass.
